note: One §4.1c mutation per rendered marker, in both families: `markers` are the data-verdict outcomes, `claims` are the data-claim measurements. A kill counts only when the unmutated baseline passed in the same run and the failure is that marker's own assertion, and every record's assertion must go through expectVerdict/expectClaim so words, value and painted state are one claim. Recorded failures are in the commit body.

tree-point.renders: #tree-verdict — ONE LIT POINT AT α = n
tree-point.computedFrom: evaluateAll(k0) XOR evaluateAll(k1), reading back the lit index
tree-point.mutation: src/dpf/gen.ts — flip every direction bit: ((alpha >>> (domainBits - level - 1)) & 1) becomes (((alpha >>> (domainBits - level - 1)) & 1) ^ 1)
tree-point.expectedFlip: point lands at 15 - α, so data-status becomes alarm and the text becomes POINT AT THE WRONG INDEX

single-share.renders: #collusion-view verdict with the collusion toggle off — ONE KEY ONLY · k0 alone lights n of 16 leaves
single-share.mutation: src/attack/single-view.ts — namesAPoint: lit === 1 becomes namesAPoint: lit >= 1
single-share.expectedFlip: a share lighting ~8 leaves is reported as naming a point, so data-status becomes alarm and the plate turns red

collusion-recovery.renders: #collusion-view verdict with the collusion toggle on — SERVER SEES α = n
collusion-recovery.computedFrom: collude(k0, k1).alpha compared with the client's secret α
collusion-recovery.mutation: src/attack/collude.ts — alpha: lit[0][0] becomes alpha: (lit[0][0] + 1) % reconstruction.length
collusion-recovery.expectedFlip: recovered index no longer equals α, so data-status becomes mismatch and the text becomes JOIN MISSED

server-view-0.renders: first #privacy-verdicts tile — Server 0 · one party-0 key of 290 B · folded n of 65,536 records
server-view-0.computedFrom: deserializeKey(keys[0]).party, keys[0].length, and fold0.foldedRecords from the real fold
server-view-0.mutation: src/pir/server.ts — in serverAnswerProgressive, if (share[index] === 0) continue becomes if (share[index] === 0 || index !== 0) continue
server-view-0.expectedFlip: the server folds at most the first record, so folded > 1 fails and data-status becomes alarm

server-view-1.renders: second #privacy-verdicts tile — Server 1 · one party-1 key of 290 B · folded n of 65,536 records
server-view-1.computedFrom: deserializeKey(keys[1]).party, keys[1].length, and fold1.foldedRecords from the real fold
server-view-1.mutation: src/dpf/serialize.ts — bytes[0] = (key.party << 7) | key.domainBits becomes bytes[0] = key.domainBits, dropping the party bit from the wire format
server-view-1.expectedFlip: server 1's key deserializes as party 0, so only this tile's data-status becomes alarm while server-view-0 stays pass

collusion-state.renders: third #privacy-verdicts tile — Collusion is off / Collusion is ON
collusion-state.computedFrom: the live state of #collusion-toggle at fetch time
collusion-state.mutation: src/ui/app.ts — const colluding = element<HTMLInputElement>('collusion-toggle').checked becomes const colluding = false
collusion-state.expectedFlip: a fetch run with collusion switched on still reports the tile as pass

record-match.renders: #record-verdict — RETRIEVED · byte-for-byte match with shelf[α] / RETRIEVED — AND WRONG
record-match.computedFrom: sameBytes(reconstruct(answer0, answer1), shelf[α]) and the differing byte count
record-match.mutation: src/ui/app.ts — verdict.className = `verdict ${matches ? 'verdict-pass' : 'verdict-alarm'}` becomes verdict.className = 'verdict verdict-pass', pinning the plate green while data-status and the words still follow the run
record-match.expectedFlip: a corrupted record is announced as RETRIEVED — AND WRONG on a green pass plate; expectVerdict's tone assertion fails where the old text-and-status assertions both passed

no-authentication.computedFrom: whether a tampered answer reconstructed to something other than shelf[α] with no error raised
no-authentication.expectedFlip: the tampered run matches shelf[α], so data-status becomes contradicted rather than alarm

dpf-key-bytes.renders: #key-byte-label in the meter — 290 bytes beside the DPF bar
dpf-key-bytes.computedFrom: serializeKey(generateDpf(0, domainBits)[0]).length for the domain under test
dpf-key-bytes.mutation: src/ui/app.ts — renderClaim('key-byte-label', serialized.length, `${serialized.length.toLocaleString()} bytes`) becomes renderClaim('key-byte-label', parts.correctionWords, `${parts.correctionWords.toLocaleString()} bytes`)
dpf-key-bytes.expectedFlip: the meter states the correction-word region as the whole key, so the claim no longer equals the measured hex dump

chor-query-bytes.mutation: src/ui/app.ts — const chorBytes = domainSize / 8 becomes const chorBytes = domainSize / 4
chor-query-bytes.expectedFlip: the baseline claims two bits per record, so chor * 8 no longer equals the domain size it names

key-part-root.renders: #part-root in the parts list — 17 B of root material
key-part-root.computedFrom: serializedKeyParts(domainBits).rootMaterial, checked against the header byte plus the root seed in the dump
key-part-root.mutation: src/ui/app.ts — renderClaim('part-root', parts.rootMaterial, `${parts.rootMaterial} B`) becomes renderClaim('part-root', parts.rootMaterial - 1, `${parts.rootMaterial - 1} B`). The deeper serializer mutation (ROOT_MATERIAL_BYTES = SECURITY_BYTES) was run first and rejected as evidence: it stops the key round-tripping and takes the whole suite red, which is not a readable kill on this marker.
key-part-root.expectedFlip: root material is claimed as 16 B against the 17 B that λ, measured from the per-level slope, requires, and the parts stop accounting for the measured total

key-part-levels.renders: #part-levels in the parts list — 272 B of per-level corrections
key-part-levels.computedFrom: serializedKeyParts(domainBits).correctionWords, checked against the words actually present in the dump, summed
key-part-levels.mutation: src/ui/app.ts — renderClaim('part-levels', parts.correctionWords, `${parts.correctionWords} B`) becomes renderClaim('part-levels', parts.correctionWords + perLevel, `${parts.correctionWords + perLevel} B`)
key-part-levels.expectedFlip: the parts list claims one correction word more than the key carries, so the summed per-level cost no longer matches and the parts stop accounting for the total

key-part-final.renders: #part-final in the parts list — 1 B of final correction
key-part-final.computedFrom: serializedKeyParts(domainBits).finalCorrection, the single byte holding the output correction bit
key-part-final.mutation: src/ui/app.ts — renderClaim('part-final', parts.finalCorrection, `${parts.finalCorrection} B`) becomes renderClaim('part-final', 2, '2 B')
key-part-final.expectedFlip: the tail is claimed as two bytes, so the stride walk loses a correction word and the parts overshoot the measured total

key-bytes-total.renders: #key-bytes in the parts list — the measured total, 290 B
key-bytes-total.computedFrom: serializeKey(...).length, checked against the length of the rendered hex dump
key-bytes-total.mutation: src/ui/app.ts — renderClaim('key-bytes', serialized.length, `${serialized.length} B`) becomes renderClaim('key-bytes', serialized.length - 1, `${serialized.length - 1} B`)
key-bytes-total.expectedFlip: the measured total disagrees by one byte with the hex dump it is measured from

key-size-formula.computedFrom: the same measured parts, restated as the size law for the domain under test
key-size-formula.mutation: src/ui/app.ts — the formula's `= ${parts.total} bytes` becomes the literal `= 290 bytes`
key-size-formula.expectedFlip: the formula is correct only at the default 65,536-record domain and states 290 bytes at every other one; invisible until the walk visits all four domain options

prg-node-width.renders: #prg-width in the trace strip — AES-128-CTR → 2(λ + 1) = 258 bits per node
prg-node-width.computedFrom: a real expandSeed() of the all-zero seed: both child seeds plus the two control bits
prg-node-width.mutation: src/ui/app.ts — const nodeWidthBits = (zeroExpansion.leftSeed.length + zeroExpansion.rightSeed.length) * 8 + 2 becomes the same expression without + 2
prg-node-width.expectedFlip: the node width drops the two control bits and claims 256, against 2(λ + 1) derived from the per-level slope the key sizes measured
